member.summary: A templated control that plays IIS Smooth Streaming content (on-demand and live), adapting the downloaded video bitrate to network and playback conditions. It wraps a MediaElement from its control template and exposes a MediaElement-like API plus Smooth Streaming features such as track selection, trick play, live position control and ad clip scheduling.

remarks.para: Typical setup: place the control in XAML (give it a Name; it is used as the instance identifier in logs and traces), optionally set , and , then set to the manifest URL (for example http://server/video.ism/Manifest). Sources set before the template is applied are held and opened when the template's media element becomes available.
On this platform progressive (non-Smooth) playback through is not supported; use a plain MediaElement for progressive files.

Event order for a new source: (optional), (the place to restrict or select tracks and streams), then . All public events are raised on the UI thread. Most members must be called from the UI thread; several throw UnauthorizedAccessException otherwise.
To control bitrate, use inside the ManifestReady handler or at any time; the built-in heuristics then switch only among the allowed tracks.
Engine tuning settings are read from an embedded default configuration, optionally overridden by the XML file named by , when the template is applied.

member.name: T:Microsoft.Web.Media.Diagnostics.Tracing
member.summary: Static diagnostic tracing facility used by the Smooth Streaming client; applications can read its output and add their own entries.

remarks.para: Tracing is disabled until a configuration with enabled="true" on its TracingConfiguration root element is loaded. The player tries to load TracingConfig.xml from the application package automatically the first time a control template is applied; you can also call one of the ReadTraceConfig overloads. The configuration selects areas, levels and destinations and the fields included in formatted output.

An entry is recorded only when its area, its level and at least one destination are enabled. The Memory destination keeps the most recent entries for ; Console writes formatted lines to the console; RemoteServer posts the memory history as XML to every seconds.
